whatIsDash.question: What is Dash?
whatIsDash.answer: Dash is an open-source cryptocurrency that was forked from Bitcoin in January 2014. The name "Dash" comes from "Digital Cash." It focuses on being a fast, cheap global payments network with features like InstantSend (transactions confirm in 1-2 seconds), optional privacy through PrivateSend, and extremely low fees (typically $0.01-$0.02 per transaction).

whoInvented.question: Who invented Dash?
whoInvented.answer: Based on the Bitcoin project, Dash was launched on January 18, 2014 by founder Evan Duffield. The first few years of development saw Dash develop a focus on speed and fungibility, making it an excellent and practical alternative to cash, both online and at the point of sale in shops and restaurants.

whatUsedFor.question: What is Dash used for?
whatUsedFor.answer: Dash is used for fast, private, and low-cost payments both online and at physical point-of-sale locations. It's designed to work like digital cash — transactions confirm in seconds and can be immediately spent by the recipient. Dash is also used for cross-border payments, remittances, and as a store of value in regions with unstable local currencies.

whoControls.question: Who controls Dash?
whoControls.answer: No single entity controls Dash. It operates as one of the world's oldest Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAO). Decisions are made collectively by masternode operators who vote on proposals for network changes, marketing, and development. The network self-funds through a treasury system that allocates 10% of block rewards to approved projects.

wallet.title: Wallet
wallet.content: A digital wallet is a software program or physical device that stores your cryptocurrency keys and allows you to send and receive digital currency.

p2p.title: P2P
p2p.content: Peer-to-peer (P2P) refers to the direct exchange of cryptocurrency between individuals without an intermediary, like a bank or centralized exchange.

publicAddress.title: Public Address
publicAddress.content: A public address is a cryptographic hash of a public key, serving as an identifier that can be shared to receive cryptocurrency transactions.

exchange.title: [CryptoCurrency] Exchange
exchange.content: A cryptocurrency exchange is an online platform where you can buy, sell, and trade cryptocurrencies using fiat money or other digital currencies.

qrCode.title: QR Code
qrCode.content: A Quick Response code that contains a wallet address and can optionally include a payment amount, making cryptocurrency transactions quick and easy.

block1.title: Lower Transaction Fees
block1.description: At the top of the list is lower transaction fees. The costs incurred from traditional payment system fees can add up. These costs can be significantly reduced by accepting a cryptocurrency like Dash. <highlight>Credit card processing fees can cost a business between 1.5% to 3.5% of each transaction's total. Transactions that are considered "high-risk" may be hit with even higher rates per transaction</highlight> (ie: card not present, gambling, cannabis, etc.). With crypto, depending on the coin, the same costs can be reduced down to mere cents -- regardless of merchant category.

block2.title: No Chargebacks
block2.description: Accepting crypto payments also means no chargebacks, which can be incredibly costly to businesses – both in regard to the monetary value and time. <highlight>A chargeback can cost your business the price of the item being disputed, as well as the chargeback fees incurred, and the time needed to dispute fraudulent chargebacks.</highlight> No centralized institution can reverse the crypto payments made to your business. Your business can choose to set up refund policies on your own terms.

transactions.quote: With Dash, accepting crypto payments is as <bold>easy as spending your profit.</bold>

createDashpay.title: How to Create a Dashpay
createDashpay.content: Download the DashPay app from the official app stores (Google Play Store or Apple App Store). Check the developer name matches 'Dash Core Group' and verify the app has significant download numbers and positive reviews. Follow the in-app setup wizard to create your wallet.

addingFunds.title: Adding funds to Dashpay
addingFunds.content: Once you've installed DashPay, you can add funds by receiving Dash from another wallet, purchasing Dash through a supported exchange, or having someone send Dash to your wallet address or DashPay username.

assistance.title: Need Assistance?
assistance.content: If you need help setting up your wallet, visit the Dash support page or join the Dash Discord community where helpful volunteers can assist you with any questions.

sendReceive.title:
How to Send &
Receive Dash
sendReceive.paragraph1: The easiest way to receive Dash as a payment from your customers is by showing them a QR code that they can scan. Both your public address and the associated QR code can be seen/copied by clicking the Receive button in the DashPay app. If you buy Dash at an exchange that is not already integrated with your DashPay app, you just need to know your public address to transfer your digital cash to the app.
sendReceive.paragraph2: There are a few ways to send Dash from your DashPay, the easiest way is by scanning a QR code. This is done by clicking the Scan to Send button in the app.

createAccount.title: Create an Account on a Reputable Crypto/Fiat exchange
createAccount.content: Sign up on a regulated and well-known exchange such as Kraken, Binance, Coinbase, or Uphold. You'll need to complete identity verification (KYC) which typically requires a government-issued ID and proof of address.

howExchangesWork.title: How Exchanges Work
howExchangesWork.content: Crypto exchanges operate similarly to stock exchanges. You deposit fiat currency (USD, EUR, etc.), place buy orders for Dash at market or limit prices, and the exchange matches your order with a seller. Once purchased, Dash appears in your exchange wallet.

withdrawalFreezes.title: Withdrawal Freezes
withdrawalFreezes.content: Many exchanges impose a temporary withdrawal hold on new accounts or after large deposits. This is typically 24-72 hours but can vary. Plan ahead to ensure you have access to your Dash when you need it.

whereDoesItGo.title: Where Does My Dash Go After I Purchase on an Exchange
whereDoesItGo.content: After purchasing, your Dash sits in your exchange wallet. For maximum security, transfer it to your personal wallet (like DashPay) where you control the private keys. Simply copy your wallet address and initiate a withdrawal from the exchange.

posGuide.posTitle:
How to Choose
a POS System
posGuide.posDescription: If you've decided that utilizing a POS will benefit your processes, finding a system that meets the requirements and budget of your business is essential. Here are several items to consider:
posGuide.posAnswer: A POS system comes with many benefits, like invoicing, inventory management, etc. Depending on the POS system you select, you may have the option to install a physical payment terminal (much like the chip/card reader for credit card transactions), create invoices, receipts, generate transaction history and reports, and even automatically convert crypto to fiat (or vice versa).
posGuide.description1: While you can simply use a Dash wallet, at no cost, it may be useful to utilize a Point of Sale system.
posGuide.description2: A crypto Point of Sale (POS) system is similar to traditional POS systems utilized for cash and credit card transactions but also adds the ability to receive payments in one or more cryptocurrencies.

posAccordion.subtitle: Here are several items to consider:
posAccordion.title: How to Choose a POS System

first.title: What is a POS System?
first.content: A Point of Sale system is hardware and/or software that processes customer payments at the time of purchase. For crypto, this means generating QR codes, detecting incoming payments, and confirming transactions in real-time.

cost.title: Consider the Cost
cost.content: POS costs vary widely — from free software-only solutions to dedicated hardware terminals costing hundreds of dollars. Consider setup fees, monthly subscriptions, per-transaction fees, and any hardware purchases required.

tools.title: What Tools Do You Need?
tools.content: Consider whether you need physical hardware (a terminal), a mobile app, eCommerce integration, invoicing capabilities, automatic fiat conversion, and multi-coin support. Match the POS features to your business requirements.

setup.title: How Straightforward is The Setup Process?
setup.content: Some POS systems require technical knowledge to set up, while others offer plug-and-play simplicity. Consider your technical comfort level and whether the provider offers setup assistance and ongoing technical support.

stakingBlock.description: Dash is not a Proof of Stake protocol, but it pays part of the block reward to masternodes to perform certain work for the network. Thanks to this, some popular staking services also work with Dash. You can deposit your Dash in any one of these staking services and obtain a return in exchange for the work your coins will do for the network through these services. If you have 1,000 Dash or more, you may also want to consider starting a masternode instead and work for the network directly.

defi.title: DeFi
defi.description: DeFi, or Decentralized Finance, offers a way to participate in financial services without a centralized intermediary. Dash is available in a growing number of DeFi platforms.

custodyBlock.title:
Custody Solutions
for Peace of Mind
custodyBlock.description: BitGo and CYBAVO provide best-in-class custody and multi-sig security solutions for Dash. Whether you are a business, fund, or high-net-worth individual, these providers offer institutional-grade asset protection.

bitgo.name: BitGo
bitgo.description: BitGo provides a simple and secure REST API to integrate multi-signature wallets with support for Dash's InstantSend. Multi-Sig HD Wallets enable enterprise-grade security.

cybavo.name: CYBAVO
cybavo.description: CYBAVO provides an enterprise wallet and custody platform for digital assets, helping businesses securely manage and transfer cryptocurrency.

accountingBlock.title: Accounting & Tax
accountingBlock.description: Some of the best-known names in cryptocurrency accounting and tax services work with Dash. They provide cost-effective and easy to use platforms to comply with local tax reporting requirements.

hero.title: Regulatory Information
hero.subtitle: Dash is not a security and offers greater transparency and less risk than Bitcoin with regards to privacy. Learn more about how legal regulations apply to Dash.

fincen.title:
DCG response
to FinCEN
fincen.description: Dash Core Group supplements the original Financial Crimes Enforcement Network ('FinCEN') with this additional information with respect to the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, published on December 23, 2020, titled, 'Requirements for Certain Transactions Involving Convertible Virtual Currency or Digital Assets'.

fatf.title:
Dash Complies with
the FATF Rule
fatf.description: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) released their guidelines for countries' regulations of the cryptocurrency industry in 2019, including the Travel Rule. Dash is in full compliance with the FATF guidelines. For more information, please contact us at

security.title: Dash is Not a Security
security.description: The status of Dash as "not a security" has been validated by many entities, most recently the Crypto Rating Council which provided the best possible score of 1.0, equivalent to the score for Bitcoin. The score takes into account various points within the Howey Test to conclude that Dash has few characteristics that are consistent with being a security.
security.secondParagraph: Business compliance officers and regulators interested in speaking with Dash Core Group and/or requesting our legal opinions on the matter, please reach out to us at

kycamlBlock.title: KYC/AML Services
kycamlBlock.description: Day-to-day compliance requirements can be difficult to scale for many businesses within the cryptocurrency industry, such as KYC/AML compliance for exchanges. The largest names in KYC/AML for cryptocurrency help ensure that businesses remain in compliance. Our partners in this space provide state of the art KYC/AML services to some of the best known cryptocurrency companies, law enforcement agencies, and financial institutions around the globe.

blockchainIntel.name:
Blockchain
Intel
blockchainIntel.description: BlockchainIntel offers a REST API that provides a risk score and corresponding reasons for blockchain wallet addresses. The score is based on known profiles tied to the address owner and behavioral data such as geographic location, links to fraud, scams and known merchants.

chainalysis.name: Chainalysis
chainalysis.description: Chainalysis works to create transparency for a global economy built on blockchains, enabling banks, business, and governments to have a common understanding of how people use cryptocurrency.

hero.title: Dash Roadmap
hero.description: Dash has a long history of innovation and development, with multiple significant products and features released over the years. Launched on 18 January 2014, Dash quickly developed new features focused on speed, privacy and usability, making it ideal for use as a digital currency. Built to deliver financial freedom and shape the future of payments for people around the world, Dash has an ambitious roadmap and proven history of delivery.

cards.title: X11
cards.description: Unique hashing algorithm combining 11 different cryptographic functions as the defining feature of Dash, providing enhanced security and ASIC resistance during the early mining phase.

cards.title: Dark Gravity Wave
cards.description: Dynamic adjustment of mining difficulty on a per-block basis, solving the issues of slow difficulty adjustment that plagued other cryptocurrencies at the time.

cards.title: Masternodes
cards.description: Incentivized full nodes forming the network backbone, requiring 1,000 DASH collateral. This second-layer architecture enabled advanced features like InstantSend and PrivateSend.

cards.title: Sporks
cards.description: A mechanism for smooth feature releases without hard-forking the network, allowing new features to be safely activated and deactivated by the development team.

cards.title: PrivateSend
cards.description: Fungible currency through transaction privacy using a mixing protocol, allowing users to make private transactions by combining multiple inputs from different users.

cards.title: Android Wallet
cards.description: Mobile payment capability brought to the Android platform, enabling users to send and receive Dash on the go with a user-friendly mobile interface.

cards.title: Code Rebase
cards.description: Transition from the Litecoin codebase to Bitcoin, providing a stronger and more actively maintained foundation for future Dash development.

cards.title: iOS Wallet
cards.description: Apple platform support bringing Dash to iPhone users, completing mobile coverage alongside the existing Android wallet.

cards.title: InstantSend
cards.description: Transaction locking via the masternode architecture, enabling near-instant transaction confirmations secured by the second-layer network.

cards.title: Governance System
cards.description: Decentralized decision-making framework allowing masternode operators to vote on budget proposals, making Dash the first DAO (Decentralized Autonomous Organization).

cards.title: 2MB Block Vote
cards.description: Network consensus on capacity expansion through a decentralized governance vote, demonstrating the power of masternode-based decision making.

cards.title: FPGA and ASIC Miners
cards.description: Hardware mining support for the X11 algorithm, bringing professional mining infrastructure to the Dash network for improved security.

cards.title: Dashcore and Insight API
cards.description: Network interaction infrastructure providing developers with tools to build applications and services on top of the Dash network.

cards.title: X11 Libraries
cards.description: JavaScript implementation of the X11 algorithm, enabling browser-based and Node.js applications to interact with Dash's hashing functions.

cards.title: Hardware Wallets
cards.description: Secure key storage devices supporting Dash, providing users with the highest level of security for their funds through offline key management.

cards.title: Lower Fees
cards.description: Tenfold transaction cost reduction making Dash more practical for everyday payments and micropayments.

cards.title: Sentinel
cards.description: Governance object management tool serving as an autonomous agent watchdog for the masternode network, monitoring governance proposals and superblocks.

cards.title: DAO Trust
cards.description: Irrevocable trust ownership structure establishing Dash as the first legally structured DAO, providing a framework for organizational governance.

cards.title: Named Devnets
cards.description: Multiple independent development networks enabling parallel testing of different features without interfering with each other.

cards.title: Governance Improvements
cards.description: Enhanced proposal validation and processing in Dash Core v0.12.3, making the governance system more robust and reliable.

cards.title: PrivateSend Enhancements
cards.description: Improved collateral handling and privacy features, making private transactions more efficient and user-friendly.

cards.title: New Branding
cards.description: Updated visual identity across all platforms, establishing a modern and professional look for the Dash ecosystem.

cards.title: Uphold Integration
cards.description: In-app currency exchange capability on Android, allowing users to buy and sell Dash directly within the wallet application.

cards.title: NFC Support
cards.description: Tap-to-pay terminal functionality on iOS, enabling contactless Dash payments at point-of-sale terminals.

cards.title: New Localizations
cards.description: Multi-language and multi-currency support bringing Dash to a global audience with localized wallet experiences.

cards.title: Automatic InstantSend
cards.description: Default instant transactions for transfers with up to 4 inputs, making fast confirmations the standard experience for most Dash transactions.

cards.title: Deterministic Masternode List
cards.description: Single source of truth for validator consensus, replacing the old masternode list system with on-chain registration for improved reliability.

cards.title: Special Transactions
cards.description: Non-financial blockchain structures enabling new types of on-chain data, laying the groundwork for Platform features.

cards.title: Three Masternode Keys
cards.description: Separated operator, owner, and voting authorities, allowing masternode hosting services while maintaining owner control.

cards.title: ChainLocks
cards.description: Protection against 51% mining attacks using LLMQ-based block locking, making Dash the first cryptocurrency to solve the 51% attack problem.

cards.title: Long Living Masternode Quorums
cards.description: Scalable consensus mechanism enabling efficient threshold signing and voting across the masternode network.

cards.title: Fingerprint Unlock
cards.description: Biometric wallet authentication on Android, providing quick and secure access to the Dash wallet.

cards.title: Uphold Integration (iOS)
cards.description: Buy and sell functionality for Apple users, bringing the same exchange capabilities previously available on Android.

cards.title: Dash Platform MVP
cards.description: Public testnet (Evonet) launch giving developers access to decentralized API, user identities, and document storage for the first time.

cards.title: DAPI & Identities
cards.description: Decentralized API with user account system, enabling applications to interact with Platform without relying on centralized infrastructure.

cards.title: Naming & DashPay Contracts
cards.description: Service contracts for username registration and payments deployed on testnet, previewing the future of user-friendly crypto transactions.

cards.title: DashPay Redesign
cards.description: Unified UX across iOS and Android with consistent design language, dark mode support on iOS, and streamlined home screen navigation.

cards.title: Dash Core v0.15
cards.description: Bitcoin v0.15.2 backports bringing core updates and optimizations, along with QT wallet UI modernization and stress test enhancements.

cards.title: Dash Core v0.16
cards.description: Block reward reallocation shifting masternode/miner ratio to 60/40, signature recovery optimization, and 650+ Bitcoin backports from v0.16-v0.17.

cards.title: Platform Protocol Versioning
cards.description: Safe breaking change deployment on testnet, enabling the Platform to evolve without disrupting existing applications.

cards.title: Document Timestamps
cards.description: Creation and update time recording for Platform documents, along with binary document fields and default identity names.

cards.title: State Trees
cards.description: Merkle tree data structures for efficient state storage and verification, along with InstantSend identity funding for fast account creation.

cards.title: DashPay Evonet
cards.description: Usernames, contacts, username-based payments, profile settings, and profile pictures became functional on testnet for the first time.

cards.title: Chain Sync Improvements
cards.description: Enhanced transaction synchronization, masternode list sync on iOS, recovery phrase assistance, and ChainLock support integration.

cards.title: Dash Core v0.17
cards.description: Extended consensus group size to 100-member quorums, established RPC restrictions for Platform security, and integrated ~500 upstream Bitcoin Core updates.

cards.title: Tendermint Seed Nodes
cards.description: Network scalability nodes for Platform, along with secure state transition acknowledgement and improved error reporting.

cards.title: Validator Set Rotation
cards.description: Dynamic validator distribution via LLMQ enabling fair and secure rotation of Platform block producers.

cards.title: Cryptographic Proofs
cards.description: Light client verification support enabling users to verify Platform state without running a full node.

cards.title: P2P Layer Optimization
cards.description: 99.5% bandwidth reduction in Platform's peer-to-peer layer, dramatically improving network efficiency.

cards.title: Liquid Exchange Integration
cards.description: Credit card Dash purchasing on Android via Liquid Exchange, expanding fiat on-ramp options.

cards.title: DashPay Invitations
cards.description: Invitation system on testnet enabling frictionless user onboarding to the Dash Platform ecosystem.

cards.title: DashMate Release
cards.description: Distribution package for easy masternode setup and management, along with local network development environment tooling.

cards.title: Quorum Rotation Enhancements
cards.description: Improved load distribution and security for masternode quorums in Dash Core v0.18.

cards.title: Proposal Fee Reduction
cards.description: Governance proposal fees reduced from 5 DASH to 1 DASH, lowering the barrier for community participation.

cards.title: Enhanced Hard Fork Framework
cards.description: New protocol upgrade mechanism enabling smoother network upgrades, alongside deterministic InstantSend locks.

cards.title: GroveDB
cards.description: Hierarchical authenticated database providing efficient and verifiable data storage for Dash Platform.

cards.title: Data Contract Updates
cards.description: Schema modification without data loss, enabling Platform applications to evolve their data models over time.

cards.title: Masternode Identities
cards.description: Reward-eligible node accounts on Platform with multi-level security framework through identity key purposes.

cards.title: Storage Fee Calculations
cards.description: Masternode compensation model for Platform storage, along with epoch-based fee allocation and credit withdrawal mechanisms.

cards.title: Headers-First Sync
cards.description: SPV client implementation for Platform enabling lightweight synchronization and benchmark suite for performance measurement.

cards.title: High Performance Masternodes
cards.description: Dual-chain validator nodes requiring 4,000 DASH collateral, introduced in Core v19 to support both Layer 1 and Platform operations.

cards.title: BLS v1.0
cards.description: Standards-aligned BLS signature scheme implementation, along with Bitcoin v0.19-v0.22 backports.

cards.title: Core v19 Activation
cards.description: Network-wide protocol upgrade driven by masternode and miner consensus, including hard fork resolution and migration support.

cards.title: Treasury Expansion
cards.description: Block reward allocation expanded from 10% to 20% in Core v20, doubling the funding available for network development.

cards.title: Rust DPP
cards.description: Dash Platform Protocol ported to Rust for significant performance improvements in Platform v0.24.

cards.title: Same-Block Execution
cards.description: Zero-block proof confirmation achieving instant state transition finality on Platform.

cards.title: HTTPS DAPI
cards.description: Browser-compatible API support enabling web applications to interact directly with Dash Platform.

cards.title: Platform RC1
cards.description: Release candidate with masternode block rewards, processing fee adjustments, NFT support, and extensive security and stress testing.

cards.title: Dash Core v21
cards.description: Asset lock transactions for Platform identity funding, masternode reward reallocation for credit pool payments, and Evonode two-chain incentive structure.

cards.title: Platform v1.0 Mainnet Rollout
cards.description: Pre-mainnet community testing validated the system. Core v21 bundled activation initiated the mainnet rollout process.

cards.title: Platform v1.1 & v1.2 Rollout
cards.description: Evonode upgrade coordination and activation readiness preparations for mainnet launch.

cards.title: Platform Protocol Activation
cards.description: Community-driven genesis quorum launch activating the Platform protocol on mainnet after years of development.

cards.title: DPNS Contract
cards.description: Dash Platform Name Service deployed on mainnet, enabling decentralized username registration.

cards.title: DashPay Contract
cards.description: Username payment service contract deployed on mainnet, enabling human-readable payment addresses.

cards.title: Dash Platform v1.3
cards.description: Batch identity queries enabling retrieval of multiple identity balances in a single request.

cards.title: Dash Platform v1.4
cards.description: L2 credit withdrawals enabling masternode operators to convert Platform rewards back to Layer 1.

cards.title: Dash Platform v1.5
cards.description: Dashmate improvements for node management and SDK refinements for developers.

cards.title: Android DashPay Wallet
cards.description: Mobile wallet release with full username functionality, enabling sending and receiving Dash via human-readable usernames.

cards.title: Dash Platform v1.6
cards.description: Stability improvements, Dashmate refinements, and SDK optimization for developers.

cards.title: Core v21.1.1
cards.description: EHF resigning fix correcting quorum member reselection for smooth network operation.

cards.title: Dash Platform v1.7
cards.description: General system reliability enhancements and stability improvements.

cards.title: Dash Core v22.0
cards.description: Compressed headers increasing batch requests to 8,000, DSQ inventory-based broadcasting, multi-quorum Platform withdrawals, and onion node support for censorship resistance.

cards.title: Dash Platform v1.8
cards.description: Instant L2-to-L1 conversion replacing withdrawal queues, contested username fees allocation to Evonodes, and Rust BLS/RocksDB library updates.

cards.title: BIP324 Support
cards.description: Encrypted peer-to-peer connections with zero overhead in Core v22.1, enhancing network privacy.

cards.title: Fungible Tokens
cards.description: Platform v2.0 introduces token minting, transfer, and burn capabilities with full lifecycle management.

cards.title: Token Controls
cards.description: Token freezing, blacklisting, and transfer start/stop capabilities giving issuers comprehensive management tools.

cards.title: Creator Attribution
cards.description: Immutable artist linkage for NFTs in Platform v2.1, along with state transition optimization and the Evolution JS SDK.

cards.title: Dash Core v23.0
cards.description: X11 hashing and lock contention sync optimization, governance UI for voting, enhanced block filters, and PoSe-based Evonode banning.

cards.title: Platform Addresses
cards.description: Simplified account creation without identities in Platform v3.0, lowering the barrier to entry for new users.

cards.title: BLAST Sync
cards.description: Privacy-preserving wallet synchronization in Platform v3.0, protecting user transaction history during sync.

cards.title: Shielded Balances
cards.description: Zcash Orchard integration with zk-SNARKs enabling fully private transactions on Dash Platform v3.1.

cards.title: Selective Disclosure
cards.description: View key-based regulatory compliance allowing users to selectively reveal transaction details while maintaining privacy.

cards.title: iOS DashPay Wallet
cards.description: Apple platform release with full username functionality, completing mobile coverage for DashPay.

cards.title: Dash Core v24.0
cards.description: Extended addresses for IPv6/Tor/multi-protocol masternodes, SegWit-adjacent Taproot support, Bech32 addressing, and GroveDB integration.

cards.title: Count Trees
cards.description: Active user enumeration via aggregation in Platform v3.2, along with referenced validation for cross-document integrity.

cards.title: Token Authentication
cards.description: Purchased capability rights transfer in Platform v3.3, with composite indices and document ownership verification.

cards.title: Having Trees
cards.description: Aggregate filtering capabilities in Platform v3.4, enabling efficient data queries across large datasets.

cards.title: Smart Contracts VM
cards.description: Virtual machine execution environment in Platform v4.0, enabling developers to build decentralized applications with programmable logic on Dash.

cards.title: Inter-Blockchain Communication
cards.description: IBC protocol implementation in Platform v5.0, enabling cross-chain asset transfers and data sharing with other blockchain networks.

bugBounty.title: Bug Bounty Program
bugBounty.description: The Dash Core Group Bug Bounty Program allows developers to discover and resolve bugs before the general public is aware of such bugs, preventing incidents of widespread abuse.
